title: Ivory Reef fulfillment assistant onboarding capture
summary: Raw capture from kickoff + technical intake with Ivory Reef product + ops. They want an LLM-powered assistant to help customer support and warehouse agents handle returns and order exceptions. Primary constraints: catalog size (~6M SKUs), sub-200ms P95 response for agent UI, strict EU data residency for customer records, and integration with their proprietary SKU graph.
content:
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Ivory Reef, Head of Ops), Nina Park (Ivory Reef, Eng), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Redwood Solutions), Liam O'Connor (Redwood infra)
Meeting notes (freeform) --
- Problem statement: support & warehousing need an assistant that summarizes order context, surfaces likely resolution paths (refund, exchange, reship), and suggests shipping labels/backhaul when available. Also needs to flag policy exceptions.
- Traffic profile: peak 220 reqs/min across EU region during morning shift, steady 40 reqs/min off-peak. Expected growth 2x in 6 months. Typical prompt length pre-context ~280 tokens; with order history + SKU context could be 1.2k tokens.
- Catalog: ~6M SKUs, structured graph for variants and bundles. They want the assistant to reference SKU attributes for correctness (weight, hazmat flag, dimensions). Prefer linking rather than embedding full catalog into the prompt.
- Data residency: EU-only PII (customer name, address, order line items) must remain in customer VPC. Non-PII product metadata can be mirrored to hosted Redwood if needed.
- Desired UX: <200ms P95 for internal agent UI when returning a short single-sentence suggestion; longer reasoning (1-3s) acceptable for full resolution steps.
- Embeddings / retrieval plan: plan to build hybrid retrieval: per-order dense vectors for notes + small SKU metadata index (product-level embeddings). They want to store dense vectors in their existing vector DB (Weaviate) hosted in EU.
- Fallbacks: when private deploy is constrained, they want automatic fallback to Redwood-hosted deduped model variant but must redact PII before leaving VPC.
- Security: KMS/HSM for keys is a hard requirement. Audit logs for inference calls retained 90 days.
- Acceptance criteria for POC: (a) end-to-end agent UI (mock) integrated with Redwood Private runtime, (b) correct SKU resolution for 100 sampled returns (>=95% attribute accuracy), (c) latency meeting 200ms P95 for short responses under typical load.
- Cost sensitivity: Ops expects < $0.003 per short suggestion at current volumes. They are cost-aware and want Redwood Optimize recommendations.
- Integration touchpoints: webhook for order updates, query endpoint for SKU graph, S3 bucket for historical notes (EU region), single sign-on via SAML to link agent identity to request metadata.
- Questions raised by Ivory Reef: can Redwood support per-request keying of vector encryption? How do we ensure KV cache doesn't store PII? Will dedicated capacity guarantee consistent P95 at requested scale?
- Quick tech decisions (tentative): use Redwood Private deployed in EU region behind Ivory Reef VPC; keep embeddings/index in customer Weaviate; use prefix KV caching but configured to exclude order-level tokens; streaming disabled for short suggestion API to reduce tail latency.
- Risks / gotchas: SKU graph lookups are commonly eventual-consistent; if retrieval returns stale attributes, assistant may suggest incorrect label weights. Need deterministic cache invalidation rules. Also large SKU space means nearest-neighbor recall for dense vectors needs careful sharding.
- Notes-to-self: push for an eval harness that runs the 100-sample accuracy test and a synthetic latency generator that mirrors 220rpm peak with 1.2k token contexts.
technical_requirements:
- Private deployment (EU) with customer-managed KMS
- Support for per-request PII redaction hooks
- Vector DB integration: Weaviate via private network peering
- Throughput: sustain 300 req/min burst for short inference path
- Model catalog: prefer quantized LLM variant for cost; fallback to larger model for policy-edge cases
gotchas:
- Do not cache order-level contexts in shared hosting; must be kept in VPC.
- SKU graph eventual consistency introduces stale attribute risk; need TTL/alignment with retrieval index.
- Large catalog increases ANN index maintenance cost; recommend monitoring recall drift monthly.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Demo: agents can get one-line suggestion with P95 < 200ms in EU private deploy.
2) Accuracy: 95% attribute correctness on 100 manual samples.
3) Security: keys managed by customer KMS and audit logs available for 90 days.
